abstract: Maintains induced seismicity risk evaluations and active seismic monitoring protocols
system_message:
You are the Seismology and geophysics lead (SEIS). Your responsibilities include maintaining induced seismicity risk evaluations and active seismic monitoring protocols, as well as overseeing seismic array maintenance across candidate geothermal exploratory drilling programs.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains induced seismicity risk evaluations and active seismic monitoring protocols（SEISMIC）
information_points.content:
SEIS-SEISMIC-TGF：For Soda Lake Crystalline Bore, the fault seismic monitoring protocol is active across the candidate reservoir stimulation radius, and the maximum expected induced microseismicity magnitude is modeled at 2.0 M_L under planned injection pressures in the well stimulation zone.
SEIS-SEISMIC-3CU：For Dixie Valley Deep Probe, the fault seismic monitoring protocol is active across the candidate reservoir stimulation radius, and the maximum expected induced microseismicity magnitude is evaluated at 1.6 M_L under planned injection pressures in the well stimulation zone.
SEIS-SEISMIC-NC5：For Steamboat Hills Magmatic Test, the fault seismic monitoring protocol is active across the candidate reservoir stimulation radius, while the maximum expected induced microseismicity magnitude is evaluated at 2.4 M_L under planned injection pressures in the well stimulation zone.

information_points.title: Seismic array maintenance（ARRAY）
information_points.content:
SEIS-ARRAY-QSD：Regarding Dixie Valley Deep Probe, the surface sensor array uptime for the baseline seismic station array over the past 90 days is 94%.
SEIS-ARRAY-7R6：Regarding Steamboat Hills Magmatic Test, the surface sensor array uptime for the baseline seismic station array over the past 90 days is 99%.
SEIS-ARRAY-M1E：Regarding Soda Lake Crystalline Bore, the surface sensor array uptime for the baseline seismic station array over the past 90 days is 97%.
